what_its_for: Acetic acid ear drops are used to treat infections of the outer ear canal (also called swimmer's ear or otitis externa). The medicine works by stopping the growth of bacteria and fungi that cause ear infections.
how_to_take: This medicine is placed directly into the ear canal as drops. Before using, warm the bottle by holding it in your hands for 1 to 2 minutes — this helps prevent dizziness. Lie on your side or tilt your head so the infected ear faces up. Gently pull the earlobe up and back (for adults) or down and back (for children) to straighten the ear canal. Place the correct number of drops into the ear. Stay lying down or keep your head tilted for about 5 minutes so the drops can reach deep into the ear. You may gently place a small piece of cotton in the ear opening to keep the drops in place. Do not touch the dropper tip to your ear or any surface to avoid contamination.
dosing: The usual adult and child dose is 3 to 5 drops placed into the affected ear every 4 to 6 hours. Your doctor may adjust the number of drops and how often you use them. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Treatment typically lasts 5 to 7 days.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the drops as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and out of the reach of children. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Do not use these ear drops if you have a hole (perforation) in your eardrum, or if you have ear tubes (tympanostomy tubes), unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe. Avoid getting the drops in your eyes. Do not use cotton swabs inside the ear canal. Try to keep the infected ear dry — avoid swimming and limit water exposure in the ear while being treated.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: increased pain, swelling, or redness in or around the ear; discharge or bleeding from the ear; fever; hearing loss or changes; dizziness or ringing in the ear; a rash or allergic reaction such as itching, hives, or difficulty breathing; or if your symptoms do not improve after 5 to 7 days of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel some improvement within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. It is very important to use all doses for the full course of treatment even if you feel better early, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
special_populations: Children: Safe to use in children under a doctor's guidance, but use with caution and follow dosing instructions carefully. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Elderly patients: No special dose changes are usually needed, but check with your doctor if you have any concerns.
